cases.excerpt: Mass spectrometry was performed on baseline serum samples collected from 173 lethal prostate cancer cases and 519 controls enrolled in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening trial.

effect_size.excerpt: Lethal prostate cancer risk increased across quartiles of choline in a dose-dependent fashion ( P -trend: 0.005), a trend not observed with increasing quartiles of betaine ( P -trend: 0.11). Higher baseline serum levels of carnitine were inconsistently associated with lethal prostate cancer in this model, with only Q2 (OR: 1.95; 95% CI, 1.12–3.39) and Q4 (OR: 2.00; 95% CI, 1.13–3.56) achieving statistical significance ( P -trend: 0.08).
effect_size.location: Results, paragraph beginning “The association between nutrient precursors”

confidence_interval.location: Results, paragraph beginning “The association between nutrient precursors”

disease_scope_review.endpoint_excerpt: Baseline serum levels of choline, carnitine, betaine, γ-butyrobetaine, crotonobetaine, phenylacetylglutamine, hippuric acid, and p-cresol sulfate were quantified and analyzed by quartile. Conditional multivariable logistic regression analysis associated analyte levels with lethal prostate cancer incidence after adjusting for body mass index and PSA.
disease_scope_review.reason: The abstract establishes carnitine as an analyte evaluated for lethal prostate cancer incidence, although the row's numerical carnitine estimate comes from supplied full-text evidence.

endpoint_case_count.reason: The carnitine estimate concerns incident lethal prostate cancer in the same case-control population, which included 173 lethal cases.

summary_html:
No matching published aggressive prostate cancer baseline is available. These saved summaries use the HR ≈ RR ≈ OR identity approximation; provide incidence in Settings for baseline-dependent calculations.
